summary:
In 2012, NASA upgraded its fire-monitoring optics from MODIS (1 km) to VIIRS (375 m), making it look like the planet was suddenly burning 3x faster—when it wasn't. **ZEPHAERIX** is a Hybrid AI and cross-sensor radiometry platform that eliminates this artificial spike, harmonizing 26 years (2000–2026) of NASA FIRMS telemetry across Terra, Aqua, SNPP, and NOAA-20 into one continuous global record.

By calibrating differences in spatial resolution, overpass timing, and viewing geometry, "ZEPHAERIX"  turns fragmented satellite archives into clear, apples-to-apples intelligence. Users can explore unified fire trends through a mission-control interface featuring an interactive 3D Blue Marble globe, a 2D timeline map, a 2000–2026 Burning Calendar Grid, automated anomaly indices, and a 2FA-secured gateway for emergency authorities.

Free from hardware-induced distortion, climate scientists, forestry agencies, and policymakers finally have a true multi-decade baseline to separate real climate-driven wildfire escalation from satellite upgrades and deploy mitigation resources where they matter most.

In 2012, NASA upgraded its fire-monitoring optics from MODIS (1 km) to VIIRS (375 m), making it look like the planet was suddenly burning 3x faster—when it wasn't. Zephaerix is a Hybrid AI and cross-sensor radiometry platform that eliminates this artificial spike, harmonizing 26 years (2000–2026) of NASA FIRMS telemetry across Terra, Aqua, SNPP, and NOAA-20 into one continuous global record.

By calibrating differences in spatial resolution, overpass timing, and viewing geometry, Zephaerix turns fragmented satellite archives into clear, apples-to-apples intelligence. Users can explore unified fire trends through a mission-control interface featuring an interactive 3D Blue Marble globe, a 2D timeline map, a 2000–2026 Burning Calendar Grid, automated anomaly indices, and a 2FA-secured gateway for emergency authorities.

Free from hardware-induced distortion, climate scientists, forestry agencies, and policymakers finally have a true multi-decade baseline to separate real climate-driven wildfire escalation from satellite upgrades and deploy mitigation resources where they matter most.

Project Details

What does it do, and how does it work?

Zephaerix is a web-based, mission-control analytics platform that solves a major historical challenge in climate science: sensor transition discontinuity. In 2012, NASA transitioned its active-fire Earth observation satellites from MODIS (1 km resolution) to VIIRS (375 m resolution). The 3x higher optical sensitivity of VIIRS caused recorded hotspot counts to artificially surge, making it appear that global wildfires had tripled—when in reality, the satellites were simply spotting smaller, cooler burns that MODIS had previously missed. This hardware discrepancy distorts long-term climate modeling and confuses policy decisions.

Zephaerix resolves this "sensor jump" using a Hybrid AI & Radiometry Calibration Core:

  1. Multi-Satellite Ingestion: Ingests 26 years (2000–2026) of active-fire telemetry from the NASA FIRMS Archive (Vol. 26), pulling data across Terra, Aqua, SNPP, and NOAA-20.
    • Area of Interest (AOI) Selector: Draw custom Lat/Lon bounding boxes or select regional presets to retrieve calibrated local histories instantly.
    • Interactive 3D Globe & 2D Map: Powered by WebGL, rendering live satellite orbital tracks and 26 years of fire hotspots on a historical timeline scrubber.
    • Burning Calendar Grid (2000–2026): Translates over two decades of normalized telemetry into an interactive multi-year matrix.
    • Key Indices & Analytics: Automatically tracks calibrated fire trends, baseline Anomaly %, and shifting fire regimes.

What benefits does it have?

  • An Accurate Multi-Decade Baseline: Gives researchers a true 26-year environmental timeline by removing hardware-induced fire surges.
  • Low Computational Barriers: Heavy cross-sensor calibrations run server-side, allowing teams anywhere to extract normalized fire metrics instantaneously in a browser.
  • Streamlined Triage: Unifies 3D spatial visualizers, 2D maps, and multi-year calendar matrices in one interface, accelerating localized anomaly investigations.
  • High-Security Access: Role-based authentication and a 2FA Security Terminal allow disaster response agencies to safely coordinate dispatch and protect sensitive operational boundaries.

What is the intended impact?

  • Climate Science: Protects long-term environmental models from corrupted baselines, ensuring predictions on carbon emissions, global warming, and fire behavior remain scientifically sound.
  • Environmental Policy: Equips policymakers with data-backed historical baselines to allocate mitigation budgets and measure true climate-driven fire escalation.
  • Emergency Dispatch: Provides forestry and disaster authorities with a secure operational dashboard to benchmark threats and deploy resources to areas facing real, accelerating danger.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software were used?

  • Frontend: React.js, TailwindCSS, and Vite for the responsive, high-contrast mission-control HUD interface.
  • Mapping & Visualization: WebGL / Three.js for the interactive 4K Blue Marble 3D Globe, and interactive 2D mapping layers for timeline scrubbing.
  • Data Processing & AI Core: Python, Pandas, NumPy, and Scikit-Learn for cross-sensor calibration and spatial-radiometric normalization.
  • APIs & Data Sources: NASA FIRMS Active Fire Data (MODIS and VIIRS archives) and NASA GIBS imagery.
  • Backend & Hosting: Node.js, PostgreSQL with PostGIS for spatial coordinate and time-series queries, and cloud deployment infrastructure.

How is this project creative?

Rather than simply plotting raw NASA fire points, Zephaerix identifies and resolves an underlying cross-sensor telemetry distortion through scientific calibration and interactive visual storytelling. The Hybrid AI-radiometry core merges physical modeling with machine learning to eliminate historical discontinuity on the fly, while transforming raw multi-decade tables into a tactile 3D globe, an isometric voxel calendar matrix, and an intuitive space-telemetry command center.

What factors did our team consider?

  • Scientific Validity: Carefully tuned bias-correction models so they remove the 2012 hardware jump without erasing genuine climate-induced fire spikes.
  • Multi-Persona Usability: Built distinct workflows for scientists (anomaly percentages and trend curves), emergency responders (rapid AOI presets and perimeter tracking), and policymakers (26-year visual matrices).
  • Performance at Scale: Used server-side preprocessing, spatial indexing, and client-side visual compression so 26 years of global hotspot data scrub smoothly even on standard hardware.
  • Operational Security: Designed role-based access and 2FA authentication so public-sector forestry and disaster teams can trust the platform for real-world operations.
